rules.title: General prohibition on rent control
rules.requirement: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except under strict conditions including voluntary compliance after six months, exclusion of certain rental units, and compensation to owners from municipal funds.
rules.summary_plain: Cities and towns in Massachusetts generally cannot impose rent control unless they follow strict rules including voluntary compliance, excluding small landlords and high-rent units, and compensating owners.
rules.summary_plain_es: Las ciudades y pueblos en Massachusetts generalmente no pueden imponer control de rentas a menos que sigan reglas estrictas que incluyen cumplimiento voluntario, exclusión de pequeños propietarios y unidades de renta alta, y compensación a los propietarios.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to all cities and towns in Massachusetts; exceptions apply only if the city or town accepts the chapter and follows specified conditions.
rules.exemptions_text: Regulation may not apply to rental units owned by persons or entities owning less than ten rental units or units with fair market rent exceeding $400.

exemption_conditions.note: units with fair market rent exceeding $400 (not expressible by fields)

rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides: (a) after six months from the date of the initial adoption of rent control regulation by a particular city or town, compliance on the part of property owners as to the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation shall be entirely voluntary and uncoerced... (b) such regulation may not include the regulation of occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion or the removal of properties from such regulation, nor may such regulation apply to any rental unit that is owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units or that has a fair market rent exceeding $400; and (c) a municipality adopting such regulation shall compensate owners of rent controlled units for each unit in the amount of the difference between the unit's fair market rent and the unit's below market, rent controlled rent, with such compensation coming from the municipality's general funds...
rules.preempts_note: State law prohibits local rent control except under strict conditions, effectively preempting most local rent control ordinances.
